insights.title: Efficiency decline tracks with Z1 collapse
insights.body: Running economy worsened from 14.12 → 14.58 ml/kg/km as Z1 volume dropped from 43% to 18% — the only month in the 5-month record where efficiency declined *while* average pace improved, suggesting compensatory muscular effort rather than aerobic improvement.

insights.title: Cadence drop in July reappears as efficiency penalty
insights.body: Cadence fell to 118 spm in July (vs 146–151 in other months) and efficiency was best (13.64); now cadence is stable at 146 but efficiency is worst (14.58), indicating form or fatigue is overriding technique — likely due to accumulated load without recovery data to confirm restoration.

insights.title: Z3 dominance masks aerobic underdevelopment
insights.body: Z3 now accounts for 33% of all time (up from 26% in Aug, 29% in Jul), yet Z1 is at its lowest (18%), meaning 82% of training occurs above conversational pace — unsustainable without verified HRV/sleep recovery support.
